sections.content:
Express Entry is Canada's online system for managing permanent residence applications from skilled workers. It covers three federal programs: the Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Canadian Experience Class, and the Federal Skilled Trades Program.

Candidates create a profile with their age, education, language results and work history, receive a Comprehensive Ranking System score, and enter the pool. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada then holds regular draws inviting the highest-ranked candidates to apply for permanent residence.
sections.title: How Express Entry Works

sections.content:
The CRS awards up to 1,200 points: core human capital factors such as age, education and language ability, skill transferability combinations, and additional points for items like Canadian education or French proficiency. A provincial nomination alone adds 600 points.

Recent draws show the pattern clearly. The October 15, 2026 Canadian Experience Class draw invited 2,500 candidates at a minimum CRS of 519, while Provincial Nominee draws cut off between 725 and 768 because nominees carry the 600-point boost.
sections.title: CRS Points and Recent Draw Trends

sections.content:
The Canadian Experience Class suits temporary workers and international graduates with at least one year of skilled Canadian work experience in the previous three years. The Federal Skilled Worker Program targets skilled workers abroad assessed on six selection factors including education and language.

The Federal Skilled Trades Program covers qualified tradespeople with job offers or certificates of qualification. Provincial Nominee Programs run alongside Express Entry, letting provinces select workers for local labour needs and adding 600 points to nominated candidates.
sections.title: Programs: FSWP, CEC, FSTP and PNP

sections.content:
Language scores offer the fastest gains: moving from CLB 7 to CLB 9 across all abilities can add dozens of points. A second language, particularly French, adds further points under the additional factors section.

More education helps too, especially a second credential or an Educational Credential Assessment for foreign degrees. Gaining additional skilled work experience, securing a provincial nomination, or obtaining a valid arranged job offer are the other major levers for pushing a score above typical draw cut-offs.
